answers.U2-S1: The passage is mainly about how trees lose their old leaves, and why some trees like maples drop them neatly while oaks and beeches hold on.
answers.U2-S2: To correct a wrong idea and introduce his main topic, which is how and why trees shed their old leaves.
answers.U2-S3: A humorous comparison, treating the trees like people who can't make up their minds or let go of things.
answers.U2-S4: Dropping old leaves takes a healthy, strong tree; weak or dead trees just keep their withered leaves on the branches.
answers.U2-S5: The beginning or start of something.
answers.U2-S6: He partly agrees growth starts early, but says it really begins even earlier, in late summer when new buds form.
answers.U2-S7: Because, like eggs, they hold new life that is already formed and just waits for spring warmth to hatch it.
answers.U2-S8: Each season prepares and gives birth to the next one, since new growth is formed during the current season.
answers.U2-S9: His own close observations of nature, like examining fallen leaves and cutting open buds.
answers.U2-S10: It sums up the passage, saying that trees get ready for spring by letting go of their old leaves in the fall.
